{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, and true outcome shows sharp drop, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.",
    "After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 10-day moving average to smooth.",
    "When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and model is flat or slightly rising, expect volatility — add 1–2% buffer for downward correction if true outcome drops.",
    "If model forecast is below 80 and true outcome rises above 85, consider sentiment-driven rebound — increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment history shows positive momentum.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently above 88 and true outcome is below 85, apply downward bias — subtract 1–2% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.",
    "If sentiment history shows multiple 0.00 entries, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for low sentiment bias.",
    "When true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast for next 5 days using 3-day SMA of true values to reduce lag error."
  ]
}
